---
title: ShinySOM
---

## Running ShinySOM

If you are not already logged in, log in to [rancher.cloud.e-infra.cz](https://rancher.cloud.e-infra.cz); see the [Rancher](../rancher/rancher) section.

By following the steps below, you can install the ShinySOM web application. This application has a persistent home directory, which means that if you delete the application and later reinstall it while preserving its name, the content of the home directory will be preserved.

### Select Application to Run

Navigate through `App & Marketplace` (1), then `Charts` (2), and select `ShinySOM` (3). See the screenshot below.

![selectapp](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/selectapp.jpg)

### Install the Application

Now you can install the ShinySOM application. In most cases, keep both `Namespace` (1) and `Name` (2) intact; however, you can select a namespace as desired except `default`. The `default` namespace is available but it is not meant to be used. The `Name` will appear in the URL to access the application. The `Name` must be unique in the `Namespace`, i.e., you cannot run two or more instances with the same `Name` in the same `Namespace`. If you delete the application and later reinstall it while preserving its `Name`, the content of the home directory will be preserved.

![appinst](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/appinst.png)

<Callout type="warn">
In the first part of the form, you select an access password. Please avoid characters like `{` and `}`. A non-trivial password is strongly recommended; however, it is also strongly recommended that you do not use a password that you already use somewhere else. The username will be `user`.
</Callout>

![appform1](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/appform1.png)

In the second part of the form, you can select the requested resources. This step is optional. The `Minimum` CPU or RAM is the guaranteed amount of CPU and RAM; the system reserves these resources for the application. However, the application can exceed the guaranteed resources up to the `Maximum`. In this case, the resources are not exclusive and can be shared among other applications. If the application exceeds the `Maximum` CPU, it gets limited; if it exceeds the `Maximum` RAM, it gets terminated (you will see an OOMKill report) and restarted.

![appform2](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/appform2.png)

### Wait for Application to Start

When you click `Install`, you will see the installation log. Once you see `SUCCESS` (see the screenshot below), the application is running.

![apphelm](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/apphelm.png)

### Login to the Running Instance

Once the application is running, navigate through `Service Discovery` (1) and then `Ingresses` (2). You will see the list of `Ingresses`. If you see `cm-acme-http-solver...` (3), wait until it disappears. Once you see `shinysom` or whatever `Name` you used in the previous steps, you can click on Target (4) to log in to the application.

![appacme](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/appacme.png)

You will see a login window; use `user` as the login name and the password you selected in the form.

![applogin](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/applogin.png)

## Delete Running Instance

If you no longer need the application, you can delete it. Simply navigate to `App & Marketplace` (1), then `Installed Apps` (2), select the application (3), and click `Delete` (4). The data in the home directory is not deleted. Running the application again with the same `Name` restores access to the home directory folder.

![appdel](/img/ceritsc/apps/ssom/appdel.png)
